LAYER 4 · THE QUANTUM SENSING ELEMENT (NV CENTER IN DIAMOND)
This is where a magnetic field becomes an optical signal. Corrected to include the microwave drive — the piece the whiteboard was missing.
a nitrogen atom next to a lattice vacancy;
its electron spin is the actual sensor
Initializes the NV spin to a known state
Swept to flip the spin; the resonance
frequency is what actually shifts with B
Field strength sets how far the resonance
splits — this is the quantity being measured
Brightness depends on spin state → photons
go to the photodiode in Layer 3 ▲
Why the field is readable optically
Resonance dip appears in red brightness;
its position on the sweep gives |B|.
the physical quantity the whole stack measures
Earth's magnetic field has spatial variations (crustal anomalies) that are:
① geographically distinct — each place has a different signature
② stable over time — surveys from decades ago still hold
③ measurable in real time — a sensitive magnetometer can read them live
④ already mapped — reference maps exist to match against
B-field → NV spin → red light → bits → B-vector → map match → coordinates → map
Green = quantum layer · Orange = sensor electronics · Blue = software · Purple = data · Indigo = user
